ingredients.name: Young/green jackfruit (polos)
ingredients.notes: fresh, peeled and cubed, or canned young jackfruit in brine, drained

ingredients.name: Roasted Sri Lankan curry powder
ingredients.notes: see sl_006 Roasted Sri Lankan Curry Powder

ingredients.name: Goraka
ingredients.notes: small pieces, soaked; can substitute 1 tbsp tamarind juice if unavailable

ingredients.name: Thin coconut milk
ingredients.notes: 1 cup, or enough to cover the jackfruit while it simmers

ingredients.name: Thick coconut milk
ingredients.notes: 1 cup, added near the end for richness

steps.instruction: If using fresh young jackfruit, peel and cut into bite-sized cubes, washing away the sticky sap. If using canned, drain the brine well.
Heat the coconut oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and curry leaves, and fry until fragrant.
Add the sliced onion and green chillies. Cook until the onions soften, about 2-3 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger and cook until the raw smell disappears.
Add the roasted curry powder, turmeric, chilli powder, black pepper, and salt. Mix well with the aromatics.
Add the jackfruit pieces and the pandan leaf. Mix well so the jackfruit is coated in the spice paste.
Add the goraka (or tamarind juice) and the thin coconut milk -- enough to just cover the jackfruit. Cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 20-25 minutes, until the jackfruit is tender.

Pour in the thick coconut milk. Stir gently and simmer uncovered for a further 5-8 minutes, until the gravy thickens to your liking -- continue longer and on lower heat for a drier, darker traditional-style curry.
Taste and adjust salt. Serve hot with rice, alongside a dhal curry and pol sambol for a classic Sri Lankan rice-and-curry meal.

source_site: theflavorbender.com, cross-checked against islandsmile.org, helafood.com, and hungrylankan.com for ingredient and technique consistency
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 5+ independent sources; strong agreement on the goraka/curry-powder/coconut-milk core with natural household variation in spice ratios
notes: Polos curry is widely cited by Sri Lankans abroad as one of the dishes they miss most -- often described as the best vegan 'meat alternative' in the cuisine, since cooked young jackfruit has a fibrous, almost shreddable texture similar to pulled meat. There are two broad styles: this version (polos ambula/curry, sour and spiced) and a milder, sweeter version called 'kiri kos' made with just coconut milk and no goraka or chilli. Traditionally cooked for hours in a clay pot over a wood fire to develop a dark, deeply reduced gravy ('borey'); the simmer times here reflect a realistic modern stovetop version. Goraka should not be substituted with plain tamarind paste in large quantities, as it changes the dish's characteristic sourness; a smaller amount of tamarind juice is an acceptable approximation if goraka is truly unavailable.
